title: Critics warned about Flock surveillance. Three Houston-area investigations are fueling those concerns.

reports.title: Fort Bend County Sheriff's Office lieutenant admits to improper use of Flock cameras per docs
Critics warned about Flock surveillance. Three Houston-area investigations are fueling those concerns.

summary:
A Fort Bend County Sheriff's Office lieutenant improperly used Flock license plate cameras to search one plate 41 times and another 148 times between January 2022 and December 2025. Internal affairs records say the lieutenant admitted the lookups were not for official law enforcement work. A resident had filed a complaint alleging the lieutenant was stalking them and that they feared for their family's safety. The lieutenant said the drivers were lurking near the lieutenant's home and family, and described a contentious familial relationship with one vehicle owner.

An internal affairs investigation found the lieutenant violated department general orders and suspended the lieutenant for two days. The lieutenant said the information was not shared or used further. ABC13 is not naming the lieutenant because no criminal charges were filed. The news outlet has contacted the lieutenant and the sheriff's office and is waiting for a response.
